A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have made a number of improvements over the current screen-reading technology and proposed a number of new techniques to improve browsing experience of visually challenged people.
the HearSay is making progress towards developing a dialog-based, non-visual browser that is more efficient and user-friendly than the existing screen readers.

we have developed a framework and the initial implementation of the non-visual Web-browsing dialog management system, which is capable of handling the basic interaction, as well as, more complex dialogs for context-browsing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Web browsing experience can be improved by using a mixed-initiative, dialog-based approach to Web browsing.
the Web can be made more accessible for visually impaired people by using a mixed-initiative, dialog-based approach.

, to make Web browsing more accessible for visually impaired people, the Web content should be presented in a dialog-based manner, and that the dialogs should be written in VoiceXML, a standard for specifying interactive dialog.
